source.title: Adoption of Fiscal Years 2027 and 2028 Biennial Budget and Fiscal Years 2027-2031 Capital Improvement Program, Exhibit B: FY2027-FY2031 Capital Improvement Program Overview
source.body: City of Berkeley, City Council Special Meeting, June 23, 2026, Item 01 (adopted by resolution)
source.pages: Exhibit B project tables pp.179-229; funding-source tables pp.170, 172-173

capital.adoption_status: The resolution adopts the Five-Year CIP "contained in the City Manager's Proposed" budget "and as amended by subsequent Council action on June 23, 2026" (packet p.6). Exhibit C (pp.249-255) amends FY2027-28 revenues and expenditures by fund; it changes capital grant revenue (funds 305-307, 336, 339) and Measure FF revenue (funds 164, 166) but prints no change to CIP project appropriations. Amendments made from the dais on June 23 are not in this packet; the FY2027 Annual Appropriation Ordinance is the controlling appropriation record and is not yet in BeTH's sources.
caveats: Amounts are budget appropriations and plans, not cash, not expenditures, not encumbrances.

prior_years and fy2026_budget are appropriations already made. Unspent capital appropriations are re-appropriated until a project completes (FY2025 ACFR, Required Supplementary Information budget note); how much of them is unspent or encumbered is not in this source.
Equipment & Fleet is a vehicle replacement schedule of the Equipment Replacement internal service fund (pp.231-247), not project rows; it is summarized in excluded_categories, not itemized.

reconciliation.category_project_counts_match_document: yes, except: Storm Water: The Storm Water tables (pp.210-212) print 13 project titles; p.212 states "14 Projects in Five-Year CIP". Dollar totals tie exactly to the printed Grand Total, so no amount is missing; the stated count is not reproducible.

Equipment & Fleet.note: Vehicle replacement schedule (pp.231-247), not project rows; value taken from p.169.

Sanitary Sewer Operation.note: Includes four Sanitary Sewer rows that print no funding source (kept as NOT_PRINTED in the project data).

Equipment Replacement.note: Project lines of fund 671 (four Fleet EV Charger projects, $6,021,000, Other Infrastructure) plus the Equipment & Fleet vehicle schedule ($33,331,116, p.169).

city_totals.explanation: Fund 621 (Permit Service Center) funds one project, "Clariti Integration With Erma" ($150,000, FY2028, Information Technology). The project and the p.169 category table include it; the p.170 funding-source table has no row for fund 621. Its group totals sum to $410,468,590, $150,000 less than the p.169 category total of $410,618,590. The p.171 chart labels Enterprise Funds $155,510,000 against the table's $155,360,000, the same $150,000. Unresolved: which total the City intends.

streets_139m.question: The $139.3 million figure is the adopted FIVE-YEAR (FY2027-FY2031) Streets CIP budget, not a two-year budget.
streets_139m.cross_check: The July 7, 2026 street plan (Tables 1A-1B) totals the Five-Year Street Rehabilitation Plan at $96,336,212 and the Measure FF five-year street program at $42,119,935 (p.8, Table 4); its fiscal impact section states the combined five-year street CIP "totals over $139 million".

adoption_changes_outside_exhibit_b.note: FY2027 revenue revised from $15,300,000 to $16,651,651 (inflator 4.95% personal income growth). No matching change to Measure FF CIP appropriations is printed.

Grant revenue revised for named capital projects (Codornices Creek, Addison Bicycle Boulevard Phase 2, Adeline, Washington Elementary/Berkeley High, Telegraph Multimodal, West Berkeley/Aquatic Park stormwater).

adoption_changes_outside_exhibit_b.note: Includes $2.5M Oxford for All design, engineering and construction and $150K Addison Street catenary lighting. Exhibit B prints only $150,000 of SOSIP money (Harold Way Placemaking).

The earlier extraction of the proposed-CIP presentation (cip-presentation.json) mixes summary labels, funding-source lines and fragments into its project list, so title matching produces false differences. Exhibit B is the proposed CIP that the June 23 resolution adopted; Exhibit C prints no change to CIP project appropriations. cip-presentation.json is kept only as a record of the earlier pass.

answer.question: How much capital funding could Berkeley redirect to streets?
answer.scope: CIP Fund 501 and Measure FF only. Other capital funds (sewer, storm water, zero waste, parks tax, state and county transportation funds, internal service funds) are not yet assessed here.
answer.short_answer: From CIP Fund 501: a gross conditional ceiling of $2,946,000 of FY2027-FY2028 appropriations ($2,916,000 excluding a contractual JPA contribution), reached only by deferring or cancelling every other project the fund pays for; neither figure is verified available cash. $10,412,200 of fund 501's FY2027 money (88%) already goes to paving. A one-time amount from unspent carried-over appropriations is possible but cannot be measured from public documents (ceiling at June 30, 2025: $11,568,647, which also funds paving and other projects already under way). From Measure FF: the adopted program already puts 45.6% into street rehabilitation, against an ordinance allocation of "approximately" 45% that Council cannot alter without voters. Whether more could go to paving without a vote is an unresolved legal question; BeTH states no amount.
what_would_complete_it: FY2026 year-end fund 501 carryover and encumbrance detail by project.
The FY2027 Annual Appropriation Ordinance (controlling appropriation record, incl. any June 23 amendments).
Public Works and Parks assessments of what deferring each fund 501 project would cost (condition, safety, legal, contracts).
The City's Measure FF maintenance-of-effort calculation and whether FY2027 draws on the Stabilization Reserve.
Restriction research for the other CIP funding sources.

Appropriated annually through the budget and the Annual Appropriation Ordinance; "Any unused funds are re-appropriated to the following fiscal year until the project is completed."

legal_authority.what: Council fiscal policy (Resolution 70,456-N.S., July 26, 2022) commits about $8 million a year of General Fund money, inflation-adjusted, to paving; it runs through fund 501 as "Street Rehab PCI Improvements".

funding_sources.permitted_uses: Capital projects as appropriated by Council. No voter or external restriction is identified on the General Fund transfer itself; the restricted portion of the fund balance equals notes receivable (loans), not cash.

classification_june_30_2025.meaning: Assigned = "intended to be used by the City for specific purposes that are neither restricted nor committed through City Council budgetary action ... Intent is expressed by the City Council or City Manager, to which the City Council has delegated the authority." Council can change it without a vote of the people or a new ordinance.
classification_june_30_2025.pages: PDF p.75 (printed p.40); definitions PDF p.103 (printed p.69)

balances_june_30_2025.derivation: assigned 16,060,094 - encumbrances 4,491,447 = 11,568,647. Encumbrances "are reported in assigned fund balance unless the purchase order relates to restricted or committed resources" (ACFR PDF p.180).
balances_june_30_2025.warning: Sixteen months old. The unencumbered amount backs capital appropriations carried forward to FY2026 and is not free money: reassigning it means cancelling or deferring the carried-over projects. FY2026 activity is unaudited until the FY2026 ACFR (expected early 2027).

appropriations_adopted_cip.pages: pp.172-173 (General Fund Resources incl. CIP Fund) and Exhibit B project tables
appropriations_adopted_cip.city_statement: "current CIP funding is entirely pre-allocated for historical programs such as those in Public Works, there is no CIP funding available for IT in FY 2027 and FY 2028" (budget-adoption p.239).
appropriations_adopted_cip.not_capital: Of the ~$4.95M annual General Fund baseline to the CIP Fund, roughly $4.03M is allocated to capital; the rest goes to personnel, debt service and other costs, and part of the $4.03M is held for supplies, survey consultants and maintenance (budget-adoption p.167).

council_authority.how: By amending the FY2027 Annual Appropriation Ordinance (Council vote). Encumbered amounts are contract obligations and cannot be redirected without changing or cancelling the contracts.
council_authority.limit_paving_floor: Measure FF maintenance of effort: if Council adopts a budget with less than $15.3 million (inflation-adjusted) for street maintenance from non-FF sources, it loses authority to levy Measure FF for two years (BMC 7.11.030(B)). Fund 501 paving is most of that floor. Moving money INTO paving is unconstrained by this; moving it OUT is.

not_to_confuse_with: Fund 164 "Measure FF - Public Safety" (a 2020 fire and emergency services tax)
ACFR "2009 Measure FF Library" (a 2008 library bond debt service fund)

legal_authority.what: Citizens' initiative approved November 5, 2024 by majority vote; adopted as Ordinance 7,952-N.S. on December 10, 2024; codified as BMC Chapter 7.11; special tax under Cal. Const. art. XIIIA, sec. 4 and charter-city authority (art. XI, sec. 5); 14 years from January 1, 2025.

funding_sources.permitted_uses: Proceeds go to "a special fund to be used only for" repair, repaving and reconstruction, safety improvements, and environmental enhancements of streets, sidewalks and pedestrian paths; plus staff costs, audits, a ten-yearly Transportation Element update and delivery review, and public art up to 1.75% of project budgets. No bicycle-specific safety improvements on Hopkins Street between McGee and Gilman. BMC 7.11.010(E)-(J), PDF p.7.
funding_sources.classification: Restricted (special tax for restricted purposes; enabling legislation). Not yet in an audited statement: the FY2025 ACFR predates collections; the first audited balance will be in the FY2026 ACFR.

allocation_fixed_by_voters.rule: Approximately 45% streets, 15% sidewalks and paths (until that backlog is eliminated), 30% safety, 10% environmental enhancements, County fees and other permitted uses. BMC 7.11.020(C), PDF p.8.
allocation_fixed_by_voters.council_cannot_without_voters: Alter the allocations of 7.11.020, expand permitted uses inconsistently with intent, or reduce the 7.11.030 budgeting requirement. Section 7(a)(2)-(4), PDF p.15.
allocation_fixed_by_voters.allocations_released_when: Citywide average PCI reaches 70 (7.11.020(D); its cross-reference to 7.11.030(C) appears to be a drafting error). Current PCI 57.

balances.fy2026_collections: UNKNOWN: the first rate covered 18 months (January 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026); FY2026 receipts and the June 30, 2026 balance are unaudited (rate report p.1).
balances.note: FY2027 Measure FF CIP ($24,328,066, budget-adoption p.170) exceeds FY2027 revenue ($16,651,651), so the plan draws on FY2026 collections. Revenue was revised up $1,351,651 at adoption (Exhibit C) without a printed change to Measure FF appropriations.

available_for_paving.what_is_established: The ordinance allocates "approximately" 45% to streets, 15% to sidewalks and paths, 30% to safety and 10% to environmental enhancements and other uses (7.11.020(C)). Council may not alter those allocations or reduce the 7.11.030 budgeting requirement without the voters (Section 7(a)(3)-(4)). The adopted five-year program puts 45.64% into street rehabilitation.
available_for_paving.what_is_not_established: Whether Council could appropriate more Measure FF money to paving than the adopted plan does without a vote. That depends on the unresolved questions below. BeTH states no dollar amount and does not conclude that additional paving funding requires a vote.
unresolved_questions: How far "approximately" 45% allows the streets share to vary, and who decides.
Whether the percentages apply year by year, over the five-year program, or over the 14-year life of the tax.
Whether the "streets" share (repair, repaving and reconstruction) is the same as the CIP "street rehabilitation" line, or also covers street work budgeted under the safety or environmental shares.
How the unprogrammed $1,351,651 FY2027 revenue increase and unappropriated FY2026 collections may be used.
7.11.020(D) releases the allocations at PCI 70 but cross-references 7.11.030(C), which concerns external funding; it is probably a drafting error, and its effect is not settled.
No City Attorney opinion or Council interpretation of these provisions is in BeTH's sources.
available_for_paving.paving_conditions: Every Measure FF paving project must include concurrent safety improvements unless Council makes a written substantial-evidence finding (7.11.060(B)).

maintenance_of_effort.rule: BMC 7.11.030(B): at least $15.3 million for street maintenance from non-Measure-FF sources, adjusted for inflation per Resolution 70,456-N.S., or Council may not levy Measure FF for the following two years. Suspended in a year Council draws $1 million or more from the Stabilization Reserve to adopt a budget, or under a disaster or emergency declaration (7.11.030(D)); reduced if an external street funding source in the 2023-24 budget declines (7.11.030(C)).
maintenance_of_effort.fy2027_floor_method: BeTH estimate: $15,300,000 x 1.0609, the factor the City applied to the $8M policy component ($8,487,200 / $8,000,000). The ordinance does not state the base year or index; the City's own compliance calculation is not published in BeTH's sources.
maintenance_of_effort.stabilization_reserve_exception_fy2027: UNKNOWN: whether the FY2027 budget draws $1M+ from the Stabilization (Stability) Reserve is not stated in the adoption packet.
maintenance_of_effort.implication: Redirecting non-FF street money elsewhere beyond the headroom would risk about $16.7 million a year of Measure FF. Redirecting other capital INTO streets only adds to the floor.
unresolved_questions: The base year and inflation index of the $15.3 million floor (not stated in the ordinance).
Which funds and budget lines count as "street maintenance" from other sources.
Whether the FY2027 budget draws $1M or more from the Stabilization Reserve, which would suspend the floor (7.11.030(D)).

restrictions.method: restriction_class is taken ONLY from a researched legal_basis in BeTH's 106-fund ledger or a cited statute/measure. Where BeTH's ledger records 'Not yet researched', the class here is 'unknown' and the amount is NOT redirectable for dashboard purposes. Fund type (enterprise, special revenue) is recorded as a signal but is NOT by itself treated as proof of restriction.

classes.voter_approved_tax: Parcel tax, sales tax or similar approved by voters for a stated purpose. Redirection generally requires another vote.
classes.enterprise_fund: Ratepayer money in a self-supporting fund. Generally restricted to the enterprise; Proposition 218 and bond covenants may apply.
classes.internal_service: Charges collected from other City funds to fund a specific service. Not general revenue.
classes.grant_condition: External grant with conditions and clawback risk.
classes.state_restricted: State-allocated revenue with statutory use limits (for example gas tax, vehicle registration fee).
classes.unrestricted: No identified legal restriction. Requires an affirmative citation, never an absence of evidence.
classes.unknown: Not yet researched. DEFAULT. Treated as not redirectable.
classes.council_discretionary: General Fund money appropriated to a capital fund. Council can redirect it by budget action, but encumbered amounts are contracts and paving amounts are bound by the Measure FF maintenance-of-effort floor.

assessment.question: What would it take to bring Berkeley pavement to PCI 60 or better, and what would that mean for the worst streets?

measure_1_network_average.what: Network-average PCI, the measure the City projects.
measure_1_network_average.reading: On the City's projections the Five-Year Plan alone falls to about 56 by 2038; adding Measure FF (about $29.6M a year, 12-year average) reaches about 62; reaching 70 by 2036 needs about $37.6M a year. These are averages over 213 centerline miles.
measure_1_network_average.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, pp.11-12 (PCI projections, Figure 1)

measure_2_condition_distribution.what: How much of the network is below PCI 50 and below PCI 25 (MTC "failed"), the measure Measure FF's goal names: PCI 70 "ideally with no streets having a PCI below 50" by December 31, 2036.

now_2024_inspection.source: City of Berkeley 2024 Pavement Management Program Update (P-TAP Round 25), Pavement Engineering Inc., April 2025, Executive Summary p.2 (PDF p.5: totals, average PCI 56), Executive Summary p.4 (PDF p.7: Condition Category Breakdown) and Section IV street list; see phase2/data/network-condition.json

assessment.finding: Reaching a network average of 60, or even 62, is not the same as eliminating failed streets. In the 2024 inspection the average was 56 while 88.5 centerline miles (42%) were below PCI 50 and 33.9 miles (16%) were below 25. The two adopted plans treat 22.6 miles of currently-below-50 streets over FY2027-FY2031 (9.4 through Measure FF, 13.2 through the Five-Year Plan), while other streets deteriorate past 50. Whether the below-50 total shrinks is not shown by any published projection.
assessment.tradeoff_the_city_published: Selecting Measure FF streets below PCI 50 instead of by cost-effectiveness lowers the 2038 network average by about one point (62 instead of 63) while treating the worst streets first (City Figure 2). The average and the distribution move in different directions.
assessment.the_adopted_goal_is_70: Berkeley's goal is PCI 70 (BMC 7.11.010(K)(1)), not 60, "ideally with no streets having a PCI below 50". The City estimates PCI 70 by 2036 needs about $8M a year more than the Plan plus Measure FF.
critical_caveats: Scenario values are the City's projections. BeTH restates them; it cannot test them without the City's deterioration curves and treatment catalog.

The distribution is from 2024 inspections, before FY2025-FY2026 paving (about 18.7 centerline miles). Plan-attachment PCIs are the values printed in July 2026 and will be lower when streets are treated.
Annual investment figures are 12-year averages including revenue growth, not flat annual amounts.
Reaching a level and holding it are different problems with different funding profiles.
